findings.evidence: Lines 67 and 71 of the same proof rewrite with `Set.mem_ofPred_eq` to reach the carrier predicate (`rw [Set.mem_ofPred_eq, Subalgebra.coe_add]`), so the lemma is available and the author knows the goal does not present in that form; lines 80 and 82 drop it and let elaboration bridge the gap instead.
findings.fix: Make both unfoldings explicit, as the same proof already does at lines 67 and 71. Line 78-80: `simpa only [Ideal.mem_comap, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, Subalgebra.coe_algebraMap] using (v.valuation_lt_one_iff_mem a).mpr ha`. Line 82: state the membership, `have h1 : (1 : S.integer K) ∈ 𝔪 := hle (htop.ge Submodule.mem_top)`, then `rw [Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at h1; simp at h1`.
findings.issue: `have this : v.valuation K ↑(f a) < 1 := …; exact this` closes a goal of the form `a ∈ Ideal.comap f 𝔪` purely by defeq (through `Ideal.comap`, `Submodule.mem_mk`, the set-builder, and the `Subtype.val` coercion). It is a `show` in disguise with no comment. The same defect at line 82: `le_trans htop.ge hle Submodule.mem_top` is ascribed the type `v.valuation K ↑(1 : S.integer K) < 1` rather than `(1 : S.integer K) ∈ 𝔪`, so unification must zeta-reduce the `let 𝔪` and solve `↑?x =?= ↑(1 : S.integer K)` to pin `?x`.

findings.evidence: Lines 203-207: `exact Nat.le_antisymm ((le_count_iff_mem_pow v ha _).mpr ((hmem _).mpr ((le_count_iff_mem_pow (integerPrimeOverOfNotMem K S hv) hfa _).mp le_rfl))) (…)` — the mirrored second argument repeats the same three lemmas in the opposite order.
findings.fix: Factor the symmetry once: `have hcount (k : ℕ) : k ≤ Associates.count (Associates.mk v.asIdeal) (Associates.mk (Ideal.span {a})).factors ↔ k ≤ Associates.count (Associates.mk (integerPrimeOverOfNotMem K S hv).asIdeal) (Associates.mk (Ideal.span {algebraMap R (S.integer K) a})).factors := by rw [le_count_iff_mem_pow v ha, le_count_iff_mem_pow _ hfa, hmem]`, then close with `exact Nat.le_antisymm ((hcount _).mpr le_rfl) ((hcount _).mp le_rfl)`.
findings.issue: The count equality is closed by `Nat.le_antisymm` applied to two four-deep nested `.mp`/`.mpr` terms with three `_` holes each, resolved only by unification against `le_rfl`. The argument is symmetric in the two rings but the script does not show that.

summary: Two spots in `integer_map_asIdeal_ne_top` close goals by undocumented definitional unfolding of the hand-built ideal `𝔪`, even though the same proof unfolds it explicitly with `Set.mem_ofPred_eq` elsewhere; and the count-equality in `intValuationDef_integerPrimeOverOfNotMem` is a four-deep nested iff-chase that hides a simple symmetric argument.
